To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
gene targeting by unmodified oligonucloetides in mouse embryonic cells is possible without induction of DNA breaks.
gene targeting by unmodified ssDNA oligonucleotids is a promising approach for the modification of genes in stem cells, and that this method does not cause genomic damage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of site-directed gene targeting by single-strand oligodeoxyribonnucleotides (ODNs) in mouse embryonic fibroblast cells and embryonic stem cells.
the development and application of novel gene targeting methods in mouse ES cells.
the development of novel methods for site-directed gene modification in mouse ESCs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ssODN-mediated correction of the EGFP gene in ESCs is a feasible and promising tool for gene therapy and that the use of PTO end-protecting groups in the ssODN should be avoided.
unmodified ssODN-mediated targeting is a very promising tool in the context of ESCs.
the use of PTO end- protected oligonucleotidies is not recommended in ESCs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of phosphorothioates (PTO) end protection for single-stranded oligonucleotidess (ssODNs), which is widely used for in vitro studies, should be avoided when targeting mouse embryonic stem (ES) cells with ssODNs.

we have shown that unmodified ssODN-mediated correction of a reporter gene in mouse ESCs is feasible, does not cause genomic damage, and that the use of anti-sense oligonucleotidess is not necessary for successful gene targeting.
we have shown that unmodified ssODN can be used to correct the EGFP gene in mouse ESCs without inducing genomic DNA double stranded breaks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the supremacy of anti-ssODN gene correction is not due to superior gene modification efficiency.

ssODN-mediated targeted integration of unmodified DNA into the genome is a viable approach for site-specific gene targeting in stem cells, provided that appropriate reporter systems are used to monitor gene targeting events shortly after exposure of the cells to ssODNs.
unmodified rather than phosphorothioated (PTO) end-protected ssDNA oligonucleototides can be used for gene targeting in ESCs.
